prize_parts.citation: For the development of targeted protein degradation, in which designed small molecules recruit the ubiquitin-proteasome system to remove selected proteins.

statement.case_for: After the first round I keep a single-part prize for targeted protein degradation (B014), with Crews, Deshaies and Ciulli. It is the only shortlisted achievement that all eight of us ranked at opening, and six of us now place it in our configuration. The scientific case is a physical-chemical one: a bifunctional molecule forms a ternary complex, and cooperativity, geometry and lifetime of that complex decide whether a target is ubiquitinated and destroyed. That is event-driven rather than occupancy-driven pharmacology, and it has held up over two decades, across many ligases and targets, in independent laboratories. Crews and Deshaies conceived and demonstrated the PROTAC; Ciulli turned it into a general, structure-guided design method (VHL ligands, all-small-molecule degraders, ternary-complex structures and cooperativity). Together they give a coherent, designed-degrader citation that can be stated precisely and defended.
statement.case_against: The credit remains imperfect. Sakamoto and Kim co-authored the 2001 PROTAC paper, and the cereblon glue lineage (Handa, Ito, Gray) is left out, which a careful reader will notice. Heterobifunctional degraders have no approval yet, so a PROTAC-centred prize leans on mechanism, breadth of confirmation and trial activity more than on a delivered drug. I accept that this is a judgement about maturity, not a proof of it. My own opening first choice, phase separation (B045), is not in my configuration because whether condensates are equilibrium phenomena is still contested.

responses.point: Linke, as chair, asks whether one citation can state induced proximity as a single principle covering PROTACs and glues, and proposes Handa as the third name.
responses.response: The principle is shared, but the discoveries are not the same kind. Handa's identification of cereblon explains how an existing drug works; it does not provide a general way to design degraders against chosen targets. A citation broad enough to include it risks becoming vague, while a citation on designed degraders with Ciulli stays tied to what was actually discovered. What Ciulli found that Crews and Deshaies did not imply is the structure-guided VHL ligand chemistry, the first fully small-molecule degraders and the ternary-complex cooperativity that makes rational optimisation possible. I would not block a Handa configuration, but I would want the committee to choose the glue arm deliberately and not by default of a three-name limit.

responses.point: Zou argues that Handa lets one prize cover both heterobifunctional and molecular-glue arms, notes that glue drugs are already approved, and says a few years' wait would cost little.
responses.response: I agree that approved glue drugs are the strongest maturity evidence in this field, and that is a real argument for Handa. But it is also why the glue story is a separate discovery with its own claim, which in my view deserves a clean recognition and not a share of a trio built around designed molecules. On timing, I do not think waiting is free: the PROTAC concept is twenty-five years old, confirmed by many independent groups, and the structural and thermodynamic understanding is mature even if an approved heterobifunctional drug is not yet in hand.

responses.point: Chabes pairs B014 for Crews and Deshaies with B042 for Liu, so that each part has clean credit and the third B014 seat goes to base editing.
responses.response: I take the credit argument seriously, and Liu alone is a cleaner base-editing attribution than the three-person unit. But the chair's question about two chemical-biology parts in one year is real for me. Adding B042 would remove Ciulli, the person whose work makes the degrader concept a general design method, in order to make room for a topic whose distinctness from the 2020 CRISPR prize I still consider open. I prefer one well-defined part over two that overlap in neighbourhood. If the committee goes to two parts, I could accept B042 for Liu alone as the second, which is why it is my first alternative.

responses.point: Somfai prefers a two-part prize of Pd-catalysed C-N coupling (Buchwald, Hartwig) and base editing for Liu alone, and openly acknowledges that B057 may look incremental after the 2010 prize.
responses.response: The Buchwald-Hartwig chemistry is clearly mature and widely used, and I appreciate that you state its weakness frankly. My difficulty is the same one you name: it extends a recently recognised class of reactions, and only four of us ranked it at opening. That makes it hard for me to put it ahead of degradation, which every member ranked. I do agree with you that Liu alone is the defensible attribution if base editing is chosen.

uncertainties: Whether the committee will choose a designed-degrader citation (Ciulli as third name) or a broader induced-proximity citation that includes the cereblon glue arm (Handa).
Whether the absence of an approved heterobifunctional degrader makes recognition early, compared with the approved glue drugs.
Whether base editing is distinct enough from the 2020 CRISPR prize, and how Nishida and Kondo should be treated, if the committee prefers a second part.
I rely on the written first-round statements and on literature knowledge that I have not rechecked; priority details of the 2001 PROTAC paper remain a judgement.
statement.conflict_note: No conflict requiring recusal. I work in lipid and soft-matter physical chemistry, which is in a general sense adjacent to lipid nanoparticles (B021) and phase separation (B045), but neither is in my configuration. I sit on the committee with Lund colleagues Heiner Linke and Peter Somfai, and I have no personal or institutional tie to Crews, Deshaies or Ciulli. This is unchanged from round 1.
